rubric.evidence: Reclassified to Case A (MDN-covered) after independent review caught a factual error in the rev-1 evidence: my initial check of the MDN position-anchor page concluded 'thin stub without Specifications/Browser-compat sections', which was wrong — a fresh fetch (2026-07-26) shows a substantive full page (Syntax, all five Values, Description, Formal definition, Formal syntax, Examples, Specifications, Browser compatibility; last modified May 11, 2026). The stub now links that canonical page and states its coverage accurately. Remaining claims trace to the csswg draft (property table + normal value definition), the ChromeStatus API record (initial none → normal; desktop+Android 151; Proposed), and BCD's granular per-value entries.
Feature id 5351959625334784 appears in the v151 milestone listing under 'Enabled by default'; route slug derives from the listing name per the documented slug rule; H1 is the listing name verbatim.

Case A stub per the mandatory Step 5 policy: MDN covers the feature (full page with Specifications + Browser compatibility), so gendn does not duplicate reference coverage. The earlier full family (property/normal/initial-value child pages + reference-contract.json) was removed before any of those routes were published — no route or identity was repurposed (check-routes PASS).

The stub's lede states the exact migration scope: behavior flips only when position-area is non-none AND an implicit anchor element exists (normal behaves as auto; auto with no implicit anchor yields no default anchor, identical to the old behavior); normal behaves as none when position-area is none. It also records that the initial applies via CSS-wide initial, non-inherited unset, relevant revert outcomes, and position-shorthand resets — not only for never-declared longhands. The earlier false claim that anchor-functions-only usage gains an implicit default while position-area stays none is gone.
The stub links the identity-matched showcase feature (anchor-default-behavior) in the quick-reference table rather than duplicating MDN's examples.

BCD per-value rows quoted exactly, including the Edge mirror entries for normal/none/auto (the rev-1 'not separately listed' claim for Edge was wrong). Value availability is explicitly separated from initial-value behavior, with the full evolution: Chrome implicit (125) → auto (127) → none (144) → normal (151); Firefox auto (147) → normal (151); Safari auto (26) → normal (27). Vendor signals (FF/Safari Shipped) come from the ChromeStatus API record, not conflated with BCD rows.

Every named source is directly linked: canonical MDN page, ChromeStatus feature + API record, csswg property definition and normal valdef anchor, BCD file, showcase feature. The stub omits the UA-style implementation-mechanism claim (no direct html.css source was cited for it) rather than asserting it from the runtime flag alone. No 'no console warning' claim (absent feature-record fields are not evidence of absence).
Single main and h1; sequential h1→h2; labelled quick-reference table with scoped headers; <wbr> hint in the long H1.
MCP matrix at 1280x800 and 390x844 verifies no document-level overflow on the stub route (pending final re-run after the Case A conversion).

The stub links the feature's own showcase route (identity-matched to chromestatus id 5351959625334784) without embedding or forking its conformance contract; the suite's cpsFeature.conformanceRoute is the feature-level route (verified 200).

openQuestions: Rev 3 (Case A reclassification): the rev-1/2 full family was replaced by this stub after independent review established the MDN page is substantive (my earlier fetch/grep wrongly classified it as a thin stub — the error is recorded here and in the rubric evidence). Child routes and reference-contract.json were removed before publication; the conformance suite now asserts the stub contract.
Local Chrome is 150 and the change ships at 151: the stub's migration statements are sourced from the spec + change record, not runtime-verified. Re-verify computed styles on a Chrome 151+ build.

The initial-evolution chain is derived by combining BCD's top-level partial-history notes with the `normal` subfeature entries: Chrome top-level partial intervals (127–144 'initial is auto instead of normal', 144+ 'initial is none instead of normal', crbug.com/501399489) plus normal@151; Firefox top-level closes at 151 (147–151 'initial is auto', bugzil.la/2030351); Safari top-level remains an OPEN partial interval ('initial is auto instead of normal', webkit.org/b/308981 + /b/311941) with the normal subfeature at 27. Caveat: Chrome and Safari top-level partials are not yet closed in BCD — recheck and re-derive when BCD updates those rows.
